newsitem.title: INDIA: India IPCL earnings seen stagnating.
newsitem.headline: India IPCL earnings seen stagnating.

text.p: Indian Petrochemicals Corporation (IPCL) may find its earnings stagnating for the next two years, Goldman Sachs and Kotak Securities said on Monday.
"Unfortunately, IPCL's earnings will stagnate over the next two years and this should cap any sustained outperformance of the market," it said in a report.

"The shares have been rather weak over past months in response to the negative impact of the Indian budget and petroleum price hikes," said the report by Paul D. Bernard and Anand Aithal of Goldman Sachs.
These measures hurt the state-run IPCL by lowering import duty rates, raising the price of key feedstock naphtha and introducing a minimum tax, the report said.
"On intrinsic value measures and on a price earnings ratio, the shares are inexpensive," it said.
Kotak Securities, the Indian affiliate of Goldman Sachs, said it was maintaining its "market performer" rating on IPCL.
IPCL was quoted at 120.75 rupees on the Bombay Stock Exchange on Monday, 0.75 rupees down from the previous close.
